name: Breadth-First Corner Peeling of Conditional Antimatroids
statement: If $\mathcal C$ is a finite conditional antimatroid, any ordering of its members by nondecreasing cardinality, equivalently any breadth-first order from $\varnothing$ with ties broken arbitrarily, is an ample-prefix order. Reversing it is a corner peeling.
proof: At the moment a member $c$ is inserted, its earlier neighbors are exactly $c\setminus\{x\}$ for extremal $x$. Intersection closure contains $c\setminus S$ for every subset $S$ of its extremal set, so those earlier neighbors and $c$ span a full cube. Thus $c$ is a corner of its prefix.
